mathematical_highlights: Unrestricted groupoid needs its own foundational size decision, not replacement with explicitly set-sized groupoids.
Quotient topology requires its preimage criterion and appropriate surjectivity scope; closed-map property is separate.
Formal unramified lifting means uniqueness when a lift exists, not existence.
Hom precomposition uses arrow reversal for first argument and explicit hom-set size convention.
Almost-sure equality is not pointwise equality; conditional-expectation martingale identity adds hypotheses.

items.original_context: Category theory: ordinary (size-unrestricted) groupoid G, a category in which every morphism has a two-sided inverse; no requirement that the object collection be a set or that hom-categories be small. Distinct from an explicitly small groupoid.
items.definition_paraphrase: A groupoid is a category G in which every morphism is invertible, meaning for every arrow f:x→y there is g:y→x with gf=1_x and fg=1_y. No smallness requirement is imposed at this abstract level, although the chosen foundations must make the object/morphism collections meaningful.

sources.relevance: Every arrow of a groupoid is an isomorphism
Detailed groupoid identities and inverses, but source uses set-sized object/arrow collections

items.mathematical_comparison_and_caveat: Groupoids are categories with invertible arrows, not necessarily small categories; Stacks detailed construction defaults to sets.

items.original_query: quotient topology on Y for f
items.original_context: Point-set topology: quotient (final) topology induced by a surjective continuous map q:X→Q, where U⊆Q is open exactly when q^{-1}(U) is open in X; includes canonical quotient-set maps and the map X→f(X) when equipped with final topology, independently of whether a larger codomain Y is surjected onto.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a surjective map q:X→Q from topological space X to a set Q, the quotient topology on Q declares U⊆Q open iff q^{-1}(U) is open in X. It is the finest topology making q continuous.

sources.relevance: Exact quotient/final topology characterization and surjectivity

items.mathematical_comparison_and_caveat: An arbitrary non-surjective map to Y has the same final-topology construction, but calling Y a quotient of X requires a scope distinction; the map to image q:X→f(X) is surjective.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: subset S of a commutative unital ring R, containing 1_R and closed under multiplication, used as denominators in ring or module localization.
items.definition_paraphrase: For a commutative unital ring R, a multiplicative subset S⊆R satisfies 1_R∈S and s,t∈S⇒st∈S.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: tensor product S⊗_R R′ of commutative unital R-algebras S and R′, with induced commutative unital R′-algebra multiplication (s⊗r′)(t⊗u′)=st⊗r′u′; the base-change algebra underlying Spec(S⊗_R R′).
items.definition_paraphrase: If R→S and R→R′ are maps of commutative unital rings, S⊗_R R′ is an R′-algebra via r′·(s⊗u)=s⊗r′u, with multiplication (s⊗a)(t⊗b)=st⊗ab and identity 1_S⊗1_{R′}.

items.original_query: natural transformations lying over identity arrows
items.original_context: 2-category theory: natural transformation α:H⇒K between functors over C whose component arrows project to identities id_{p(x)} in C.

items.original_context: Field theory: subfield F of a field E is a subset F⊆E containing 0_E,1_E and closed under inherited field addition, additive inverses, multiplication and inverses of nonzero elements of F, with induced field operations.
items.definition_paraphrase: A subfield F of a field E is a subset F⊆E containing 0_E and 1_E, closed under addition, additive inverses, multiplication, and multiplicative inverses of nonzero F-elements, with operations inherited from E.

items.original_query: sends closed subsets to closed subsets
items.original_context: General topology: a continuous map f:X→Y is a closed map if every closed F⊆X has closed image f(F)⊆Y; here it is the underlying continuous map of a scheme base change, without a Hausdorff or properness assumption.
items.definition_paraphrase: A map f:X→Y of topological spaces is closed if the image f(F) is closed in Y for each closed subset F⊆X.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: lift of an R-algebra homomorphism f:S→A/I across a surjective R-algebra map q:A→A/I, namely an R-algebra homomorphism g:S→A satisfying q∘g=f. Here I is square-zero and formal unramifiedness only requires uniqueness, not existence.

items.original_query: arbitrary direct product ∏_j Q_j of R-modules
items.original_context: Module theory: product of an arbitrary indexed family of R-modules (Q_j)_{j∈J}, consisting of all tuples (q_j)∈∏_jQ_j with coordinatewise addition and scalar action; unlike a direct sum, supports need not be finite.
items.definition_paraphrase: Given a ring R and left R-modules Q_j indexed by J, their direct product ∏_{j∈J}Q_j is the set of all tuples (q_j) with coordinatewise addition/scalar multiplication, without finite-support restriction.

items.original_query: cone arrows L→F(i) compatible with all arrows of I
items.original_context: Category theory: cone from vertex L to a diagram F:I→C, a natural transformation constant_L⇒F with compatible arrows L→F(i); not necessarily a limit cone.

items.original_query: cover of Spec(R) by standard opens D(f_i)
items.original_context: Algebraic geometry: family of distinguished opens D(f_i) in Spec(R) with union equal to Spec(R); the f_i need not all be the same and the localizations are taken on these opens.
items.definition_paraphrase: The distinguished opens D(f_i) cover Spec(R) if ⋃_i D(f_i)=Spec(R). For any family in a unital ring, this is equivalent to the ideal (f_i:i∈I) being R; by quasi-compactness a finite subcover then exists.

items.original_context: Module theory: submodule generated by a subset S of a left R-module M, consisting of all finite R-linear combinations of elements of S; for a finite S={m_1,...,m_n} this is the finite R-linear span Σ_i R m_i, possibly all of M.
items.definition_paraphrase: For an R-module M and S⊆M, span_R(S) is the submodule of all finite linear combinations Σ_{k=1}^n r_k s_k with r_k∈R and s_k∈S. The empty combination is 0.
